$doc: The loop's driver — machine-readable on purpose: readiness, batches, and
cap breaches are computed by schedule.mjs, never by eye. Append-mostly:
never delete a ticket; mark it done or decomposed.
status: todo | in-progress | done | blocked | decomposed ('ready' is computed).
files is a CONTRACT: the verifier diffs the branch and fails undeclared
touches (package.json + lockfiles allowlisted for every ticket).
attempts is the durable diagnosis log. evidence holds the INDEPENDENT
re-verify's output, not the builder's claim.

tickets.title: Story validator: screenshot-based choreography checks for any scrolly HTML file
tickets.origin: SPEC §14 + §10; acceptance sharpened per red-team (ledger [0004])
tickets.context: Read README.md (contract tables), SPEC.md §5 + §14, test/semantics.test.js (puppeteer-core patterns, Chrome path). Build `node test/validate-story.mjs <file.html> [--tier1]` printing a JSON report and exiting 0/1. RED-TEAM-HARDENED DESIGN REQUIREMENTS (non-negotiable): (1) distinctGraphicStates is SCREENSHOT-BASED — at each step's trigger position take a viewport screenshot of the story region and compare hashes; states are distinct only if pixels differ beyond a small threshold. This covers canvas graphics automatically and rejects invisible/occluded attribute toggles. (2) glueTier via RUNTIME INSTRUMENTATION, not text grep: before any page script runs (evaluateOnNewDocument), wrap EventTarget.prototype.addEventListener (flag scroll/wheel/touchstart/touchmove), onwheel/onscroll property setters, window.IntersectionObserver construction, and Element.prototype.getBoundingClientRect; attribute each call to lib vs author via Error().stack correlation with script order — AND the lib script block must be byte-identical to src/scrolly.js (read from disk), else the ENTIRE block counts as author code. tier1 = zero author calls flagged AND author scripts contain only Scrolly.init statement(s) (AST-light check acceptable: strip comments/strings first). tier2 = no flagged calls. else fail, with the specific flagged API named in the report. Words like 'wheel' in comments/strings must NOT trip it. (3) externalUrls: network-request interception is the authority (page.on('request'), anything not file:// on the fixture's own path), plus a secondary source scan matching (https?:)?// in src/href/xlink:href/srcset/CSS url(). (4) consoleErrors: attach console/pageerror/unhandledrejection listeners BEFORE goto; dwell ≥300ms after each scroll position. (5) bidirectionalConsistent: record state (screenshot hash + data-active-step + is-shown set) at each step top-to-bottom, then bottom-to-top, then a NON-MONOTONIC jump order (last→second→last→first); every revisit must match the first visit. (6) Multi-story pages: per-story reports keyed by root index/id; overall exit is the AND of all stories. (7) No fixture-name special-casing: the validator source must not reference fixture filenames. Exit-0 thresholds per story: stepCount>=4, distinctGraphicStates>=4, glueTier ok, no externalUrls, no consoleErrors, bidirectionalConsistent. Craft the broken/clean fixtures named in files (self-contained, lib inlined byte-identical from src/): dead-steps (4 steps, class churn but pixel-identical graphic), external-url (an https:// img AND a protocol-relative //cdn ref), scroll-jack (plain addEventListener('wheel')), scroll-jack-obfuscated (window['addEventListener']('whe'+'el',...) or onwheel= assignment), asymmetric-state (author stepenter draw that accumulates instead of drawing full state — passes everything except bidirectional), runtime-error (author JS throws after load), fetch-external (URL only constructed at runtime via fetch('ht'+'tps://...')), and fixtures-clean/wheel-in-comment (tier-2-clean page whose author script merely CONTAINS the word wheel in a comment — must PASS). test/validator.test.js asserts every contrast pair below, and runs each broken fixture from a COPY at a randomized temp filename (no name sniffing). If this ticket proves bigger than one session, return tooBig with a proposed split (e.g. core driver / instrumentation / fixtures+tests) rather than half-building.
tickets.acceptance:
- `node test/validate-story.mjs index.html` → exit 0, JSON report with all specified fields
- dead-steps → exit 1, report's failure reasons include distinctGraphicStates<4 and do NOT include glueTier/externalUrls failures (exclusivity)
- external-url → exit 1 listing BOTH the https:// and the protocol-relative URL; no other failure reasons
- fetch-external → exit 1 with the intercepted request URL listed (proves real network interception, not source regex)
- scroll-jack AND scroll-jack-obfuscated → exit 1, glueTier=fail naming the flagged API; no other failure reasons
- fixtures-clean/wheel-in-comment → exit 0 (comment/string mentions must not trip instrumentation)
- asymmetric-state → exit 1 solely for bidirectionalConsistent=false
- runtime-error → exit 1 solely for consoleErrors non-empty
- `grep -E 'dead-steps|external-url|scroll-jack|asymmetric|runtime-error|fetch-external' test/validate-story.mjs` → no matches (no fixture sniffing)
- validator.test.js runs every broken fixture via randomized-temp-filename copies and asserts the exact failure reason per case
- `bun test` green
tickets.evidence: Independent verify (workflow wf_d6471f1e-2ce): verified=true, no regression, no out-of-scope, no gaming. Coordinator gate on merged tree d057805: bun test 45 pass/5 files; validate-story index exit 0; all 7 broken fixtures fail for exactly their one reason (dead-steps:distinctGraphicStates<4, external-url:externalUrls, fetch-external:externalUrls via interception, scroll-jack+obfuscated:glueTier fail naming addEventListener(wheel), asymmetric:bidirectionalConsistent, runtime-error:consoleErrors); clean fixture exit 0; fixture-name grep 0. Commit bca6566 (merge of ticket/S101 b2355e5).

tickets.title: Declarative camera: data-camera/data-focus/data-zoom → --camera-transform
tickets.origin: SPEC §15.3; oracle Phase M-A

New src/camera.ts: resolve each focused step's shot — target box in the [data-camera] element's UNTRANSFORMED space (invert current matrix via DOMMatrix/getCTM), data-zoom number or default fit (~70% of stage); root-level data-focus is the establishing shot. Endpoints measured at init/step-change/resize — NEVER per frame. Interpolation in geometry.ts as pure math: pan linear, zoom log-space, across the earlier focused step's chapter progress; unit-test both incl. the k1=k2 and fit cases. story.ts emits one composed --camera-transform on the root; steps without data-focus hold the previous shot; dangling selector → hold + warn; reduced motion → snap to nearer shot (cut). scrolly.css: .scrolly.is-ready [data-camera] { transform: var(--camera-transform, none) } — geometry, so structural. HARD CONSTRAINTS: no scrollTop/scrollTo/scrollBy anywhere (validator instrumentation must stay clean); size bar (v0.4 amendment) binds dist/scrolly.min.js ≤ 4096 B gz — prior attempt measured the full camera at 3296 B gz total on min (fits with ~800 B spare); if it would NOT fit, STOP and return blocked with numbers. e2e: mid-chapter screenshot differs from BOTH endpoint screenshots (flight, not cut — anti-gaming: this cannot be satisfied by transition tuning because captures are settle-independent), reverse lands identically, resize re-measures (change viewport, assert new endpoint transform).

- unit: pan interpolation linear, zoom interpolation log-space, as pure math in geometry.ts incl. k1=k2 and default-fit cases
- e2e (motion.spec.ts additive): mid-chapter screenshot differs from BOTH endpoint screenshots (flight, not cut; captures settle-independent); reverse traversal lands identically; resize re-measures (viewport change → new endpoint transform)

Genre constraint: NOT a geographic map (examples/virus-got-out.html owns that) and NOT the flat overlay boundary-rotation piece (examples/scroll-linked.html owns R2D3's §14 choreography row). Suggested subject staying in R2D3's spirit: a decision-tree / data-space tour — a large SVG scatter that a model progressively partitions; steps fly the camera between regions (per-step data-focus on anchor elements + varied data-zoom) while data-scrub drives continuous author-@keyframes motion (points drifting to their partitions, a split line sweeping in). Creative details are yours; the choreography kind is not. MECHANICS: (a) Tier 1 means author JS is EXACTLY Scrolly.init() — scripts/validate-story.mjs classifies anything else as glue; all motion comes from CSS @keyframes + data-scrub + the camera variable. (b) Copy the marker-block skeleton from examples/scroll-linked.html (<!-- scrolly:css -->…<!-- /scrolly:css --> and <!-- scrolly:js -->…<!-- /scrolly:js -->); leave block INTERIORS empty or stale and run `bun run build` — scripts/sync-embeds.mjs injects the lib; NEVER hand-edit inside markers. (c) Fully self-contained file:// page: zero external URLs, no vendored libs (oracle locked). (d) e2e/motion.spec.ts (~line 769) auto-sweeps every examples/*.html for `scrolly:` console warnings — every data-show/data-scrub/data-focus token must resolve (no dangling refs; M205's diagnostics are live). (e) Camera-rig reference: examples/virus-got-out.html ~329-750 (data-camera stage element, per-step data-focus/data-zoom, invisible anchors are idiomatic). (f) Add one gallery row to the README.md examples table (~lines 111-116) matching its format, tier claim 1. (g) Reduced-motion degrades to cuts automatically via the structural mechanic — do not add your own reduced-motion handling. LOCKED (cite oracle.md): additive only; this ticket touches NO src/ — dist/ must come out byte-identical after `bun run build` (that is the proof of zero lib impact); no scroll writes; tier budgets bind; do not touch SPEC.md. New-behavior tests: exempt (pure-content example ticket — the §14 validator is its oracle); the e2e gallery sweep picks the page up automatically. Self-check the flight probe with a SCRATCH Playwright script (sweep scroll positions, read --camera-transform off the root, screenshot mid-chapter vs endpoints) but do NOT commit the scratch script; the coordinator re-runs the probe independently. RED-TEAM SHARPENINGS (ledger [0036]) baked into the acceptance below — read them as design constraints, not afterthoughts: the camera checks sample the RESOLVED transform matrix on the [data-camera] element (so your author CSS must actually consume the variable: `.scrolly.is-ready [data-camera] { transform: var(--camera-transform, none) }`); scrub must be visually live (no-op or invisible keyframes fail); camera and scrub must co-occur in the SAME chapters (≥2 step ids that both carry data-focus and are scrubbed against); the tour must have real magnitude (zoom ratio ≥3, pan ≥30% of stage diagonal); the piece must NOT resemble virus-got-out (different genre; the coordinator diffs token 8-grams, <30% overlap required) and carries no filler prose. Checks 2-4 of the acceptance ship as a COMMITTED Playwright spec e2e/zoom-tour.spec.ts (follow e2e/motion.spec.ts conventions for serving/loading examples; plain page tests, default project) — pin its assertions to the acceptance verbatim so reviewing the spec is a read, not an audit.
tickets.acceptance:
1. node scripts/validate-story.mjs examples/zoom-tour.html --tier1 exits 0: bidirectionalConsistent true, glueTier tier1, glueFlags [], externalUrls [], consoleErrors [], stepCount >= 8, distinctGraphicStates >= 7
2. camera-tour probe (committed e2e/zoom-tour.spec.ts) sampling getComputedStyle('[data-camera]').transform — the RESOLVED matrix, never the custom property — at >=40 positions spanning first-step top to last-step bottom: (a) >=10 distinct matrices after rounding entries to 2 decimals; (b) max-scale/min-scale >= 3; (c) max camera-center displacement >= 30% of the stage bbox diagonal; (d) for one adjacent focused-step pair, the figure-cropped midpoint screenshot differs pixel-wise from BOTH endpoint screenshots AND the midpoint matrix differs from both endpoint matrices
3. attribute floor (same spec, static DOM): >=4 steps carry data-focus; >=3 distinct focus targets; >=2 distinct data-zoom values; >=2 step ids X where step #X carries data-focus AND some element carries data-scrub="X"
4. scrub-liveness probe (same spec): every [data-scrub] element has computed animation-name != none and animation-play-state paused; for each distinct scrub id, at in-chapter progress ~0.25 and ~0.75 at least one carrying element's serialized computed visual state (transform/offset-distance/opacity/clip-path/stroke-dashoffset/geometry) differs, and at both samples the element has rect w>0 h>0, opacity >= 0.05, and intersects the figure rect
5. gallery warning sweep green on the new page (e2e/motion.spec.ts auto-discovers it; zero scrolly: warnings)
6. anti-filler floors: grep -riE 'lorem|ipsum|placeholder|tbd|fixme' examples/zoom-tour.html -> 0 hits; every .step >= 120 chars text content, page total >= 1200 (asserted in the probe spec). Anti-clone: coordinator-run token 8-gram overlap vs virus-got-out (embed blocks stripped) < 30% — self-check with a SCRATCH script, do not commit it
7. README gallery row added, tier claim matches validator; node scripts/check-links.mjs green
8. baseline: bun run check exit 0; bun run build twice -> byte-identical dist/ (proves zero src impact)
